---
title: "Install"
subtitle: "Three steps, and the first may be done already."
---

::: {.steps}

1.  ### Have an agent

    Emaki reads and drives the coding agents on your machine, so at least
    one has to be installed and signed in.

    ::: {.agents}

    ::: {.agent .agent-claude}
    **Claude Code**

    [Install it from Anthropic's documentation](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code),
    then run `claude` once to sign in.
    :::

    ::: {.agent .agent-codex}
    **Codex**

    [Install it from OpenAI's documentation](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli),
    then run `codex` once to sign in.
    :::

    :::

    Not sure what this machine has? Emaki's Agents page ([⌘E]{.kbd}) says,
    and walks through installing an agent a numbered step at a time, with a
    shell beside the steps. Git is optional: with it, Emaki shows a
    project's changes and branches and commits for you.

2.  ### Download Emaki

    ::: {.downloads}
    <a class="download" data-os="mac" data-chip="arm64" href="https://github.com/alkaline-software/emaki/releases/latest/download/Emaki-mac-arm64.dmg"><strong>macOS</strong> <span>Apple silicon</span></a>
    <a class="download" data-os="mac" data-chip="x64" href="https://github.com/alkaline-software/emaki/releases/latest/download/Emaki-mac-x64.dmg"><strong>macOS</strong> <span>Intel</span></a>
    <a class="download" data-os="windows" href="https://github.com/alkaline-software/emaki/releases/latest/download/Emaki-windows-x64-setup.exe"><strong>Windows</strong> <span>x64 installer</span></a>
    <a class="download" data-os="linux" href="https://github.com/alkaline-software/emaki/releases/latest/download/Emaki-linux-x64.AppImage"><strong>Linux</strong> <span>x64 AppImage</span></a>
    :::

    Each link takes the [latest release](https://github.com/alkaline-software/emaki/releases/latest).
    The Mac image is signed and notarized and opens without argument; it
    needs macOS 14 or later. Windows is unsigned, so SmartScreen asks once:
    *More info*, then *Run anyway*. On Linux run the AppImage, or install
    the `.deb` from the release page.

3.  ### Open it

    The first launch copies every Claude Code transcript it finds into
    `~/.emaki/archive`, and every later launch catches up, so nothing is
    lost while the app was closed. Pick a folder and type a message to
    start a session, or open one from the sidebar.

    From then on the app updates itself: from Settings, Updates, or on a
    daily check.

:::

## What it keeps

Everything is under `~/.emaki`:

| | |
|---|---|
| `archive/` | every Claude Code session, copied byte for byte, a folder an agent and a project |
| `logs/` | each session rendered as markdown |
| `search.db` | the full-text index |
| `models/` | the dictation models you download |
| `config.json` | your settings |

: {.table-keys tbl-colwidths="[24,76]"}

Only `archive/` cannot be rebuilt from something else. That is the folder to
back up.

## The one thing it changes

Emaki sets a single thing in Claude Code's settings: its own status line,
which feeds the context and rate-limit row under the composer. Nothing else
is touched, and no hook is installed. To put your old status line back:

```sh
emaki-core statusline restore
```

## Dictation

On a Mac, Settings, Dictate downloads a speech model (Qwen3-ASR or Whisper)
and, if you want it, a small language model that tidies what was said. Both
run on this machine, and nothing you say leaves it. To dictate into other
apps, allow Accessibility when Dictate asks. [More on dictation](features.qmd#dictation).

## Building from source

Rust, with [GPUI](https://www.gpui.rs). On a Mac the build needs CMake
(`brew install cmake`) for the dictation model runner.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/alkaline-software/emaki
cd emaki
cargo build -p emaki-app && ./target/debug/Emaki
```
